title: Complexity Intuition and Problem-Solving Strategies
objectives: Build a basic intuition for how much slower an algorithm gets as the input grows (O(1), O(n), O(n²), O(log n))
Know which strategies to use when facing a new problem

hook.text: You tested a search algorithm on an array of 10 elements, and it ran fast. What if you ran it on an array of 10 million elements: would it still be fast? That depends on the algorithm's 'complexity'.

concept.heading: A feel for growth rates
concept.body: O(1): finishes in constant time no matter the input size (e.g. reaching array[0]). O(n): needs as many steps as the input (e.g. linear search, summing an array). O(n²): needs steps equal to the square of the input because of a nested loop (e.g. bubble/selection sort). O(log n): the work is halved at each step (e.g. binary search), so it stays fast even for very large inputs.

concept.heading: Problem-solving strategies
concept.body: Approach a new problem with these questions: (1) What are the input, process, and output? (2) Is there a similar problem I have solved before (search, sort, counter/accumulator)? (3) Can I split the problem into smaller parts (functions, recursion)? (4) Can I start with a rough solution and improve it afterward?

steps: What are the input / process / output?
Have I solved a similar problem?
Can I split it into smaller parts?
Try it by hand: build a trace table

exercises.question: What is the complexity of reaching the first element of an array (array[0])?

feedback.correct: Correct. It is reached in a single step regardless of the array size: O(1).
feedback.incorrect: Direct access to any index of an array takes constant time no matter the size: O(1).

exercises.question: What is the complexity of linear search?

feedback.correct: Correct. In the worst case the whole array (n elements) is checked.
feedback.incorrect: In the worst case, linear search checks n elements one by one: O(n).

exercises.question: What is the complexity of bubble sort (nested loops)?

feedback.correct: Correct. Two nested loops lead to n×n steps: O(n²).
feedback.incorrect: Two nested loops need steps equal to the square of the input size: O(n²).

exercises.question: What is the complexity of binary search?

feedback.correct: Correct. The search space is halved at each step, so it is O(log n).
feedback.incorrect: Binary search has O(log n) complexity because it halves the search space at every step.

exercises.question: In an array of 1 million elements, which algorithm gives the fastest result in practice?
options: An O(log n) binary search (if the array is sorted)
They all run at the same speed

feedback.correct: Correct. For large inputs, O(log n) is dramatically faster than the others.
feedback.incorrect: For large inputs, O(log n) algorithms (like binary search) are much faster than O(n) and especially O(n²).

exercises.question: Put the thinking order to follow when you face a new problem in the correct order.
steps: Think about whether there is a similar problem that has been solved before
Split the problem into smaller parts
Start with a rough solution, then improve it

exercises.question: What does "complexity" (O notation) measure?
options: How many lines the code has
How much slower the algorithm gets as the input grows

feedback.correct: Correct. O notation expresses how the running time grows as the input size increases.
feedback.incorrect: Complexity does not measure the number of lines, it measures the RATE at which an algorithm slows down as the input grows.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.template: Operations that always finish in constant time, regardless of the input size, have ___ complexity.

summary: O(1): constant. O(n): as many steps as the input. O(n²): the square of the input. O(log n): halves at each step.
For large inputs, O(log n) and O(n) are much faster than O(n²).
With a new problem: identify the input/output, look for a similar problem, split it up, and start with a rough solution before improving it.
Congratulations, you have completed the core curriculum of Algorithm Learning! 🎉
